title: lint: the object publish door does not run validateSortableFields, so an object whose listViews sort a sortable:false field saves
body:
domain:server#6 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzibcN9oHa8kDbTTnL5

Filed from PR #30084 (card #30023), contract review PASS at `c745679c`, 2026-11-04. ⛔ Not a claim. Triage sets the grade.

Business reason: `validateSortableFields` names the runtime types `view` and `page`, but not `object`. So an object write that declares `sortable: false` on a field and also sorts on that field in one of its own `listViews.*.sort` saves through the publish door, and that list view then fails at read with `400 INVALID_SORT`. `os validate` already catches it. The runtime door does not.

Reader who acts: `packages/lint` owner (`reference-integrity-suite.ts`, `authoring-rules.ts`).

## What to do
- Add `object` to the member's `runtimeTypes`, with its own rollout decision, following the suite's #15254 note on adding an object crossing. Pin the refusal through the real object publish route, and add the lint suite member in the same PR.

Dedupe: `object door validateSortableFields`, `listViews sort sortable false`. **New.**
